results.title: Corporate cybersecurity risk and data breaches: A systematic review of empirical research
results.content: Consequences of cybersecurity risk and data breaches](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/03128962241293658#sec-5). IT expertise in the top management team (TMT) adds value: chief executive officers (CEOs) and chief financial officers (CFOs) with IT expertise are more likely to prioritize cybersecurity risk mitigation and identify critical investment to prevent breaches ([Haislip et al., 2021](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/03128962241293658#bibr89-03128962241293658)). Firms with greater financial risk (higher leverage ratios) are more likely to experience data breaches ([Pei et al., 2020](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/03128962241293658#bibr165-03128962241293658)). Technological advances, coupled with increased networks reliance and data digitalization, have heightened corporate exposure to cybersecurity risk ([Uddin et al., 2020](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/03128962241293658#bibr213-03128962241293658)). Corporate governance can mitigate market reactions to data breaches: firms experience less negative reactions when their boards have technology committees ([Higgs et al., 2016](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/03128962241293658#bibr97-03128962241293658)) and pay more attention to risk management ([Kamiya et al., 2021](https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/03128962241293658#bibr114-03128962241293658)).
